To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the proton hyperfine coupling values for Cu(2+)-(glycine)(n) complexes in single-crystal matrices are highly dependent on the dihedral angles of the amino group and the C(alpha) hydrogen.
the isotropic proton hyperfine couping values for C(alpha) and NH3 hydrogens in Cu(2+)-(glycine)(n) complexes are correlated with the dihedral angle between the CuN3 and CuN1C1 planes.

the proton isotropic coupling constants for the alpha-carbon-bound and amino hydrogen atoms in copper-amino-acid complexes can be related to the dihedral angles between the copper-nitrogen and carbon-carbon bonds.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structure and bonding of copper(II)-amino acid complexes.
the structure and bonding in Cu(2+)-(alpha-glycine)(n) (n = 1, 2, 3, 4) complexes.
elucidating structure-bonding relationships for copper-doped amino acids.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the experimental and theoretical results are consistent with a mechanism of spin transfer from the Cu(2+) to the C(alpha)-bound protons via the pi orbital of the C(alpha)-C(beta) bond.
the experimental proton isotropic hyperfines are sensitive to dihedral angles between the amino and carboxylate groups and the copper complex.

the proton hyperfine couplngs are highly sensitive to the local structure and that the dihedral angle dependence of the proton couplings provides a powerful tool for structural analysis of Cu(2+), or other metal ions in amino acid complexes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the experimental and theoretical results support a hyperconjugation mechanism to explain the proton coupling variations, but the details of the mechanism need further study.

the geometric sensitivity of the proton couplings in the Cu(2+) complexes of amino acids arises from the transfer of spin density from copper into the amino and C(alpha) hydrogen orbitals via a hyperconjugation-type mechanism, but the details of this mechanism remain to be determined.

the proton hyperfine couping variations with dihedral angle are a reflection of the structural and geometric features of the Cu(2+):ligand complexes, and that the QM calculations are useful in understanding the trends in the experimental data.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a combination of EPR/ENDOR measurements with QM calculations is a useful strategy for elucidating structure and bonding in metal-doped amino acid complexes.
a detailed analysis of experimental and theoretical proton couplings can reveal the structural features and bonding characteristics of copper-amino acid systems.
the proton hyperfine couplers can provide a sensitive measure of structural variations in copper complexes, and the isotropic coupling is particularly useful for this purpose.
